title: Snake and scorpion bites or stings
description: Bites or stings from venomous snakes, scorpions, spiders, or insects. Severity depends on the species, the amount of venom, and the person.

recognition_questions.q: What bit/stung the person? (Snake, scorpion, bee?) Try to describe it.
Is there swelling, pain, or discolouration at the bite site?
Is the person having difficulty breathing, swelling of the face, or dizziness?

immediate_safety_warnings: Move away from the snake or scorpion; do not try to catch or kill it.
Help the person stay calm and still — movement speeds venom spread.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Move the person away from the snake/scorpion and help them lie down and keep still.
Call 112, or take the person to hospital immediately. Snakebite and severe scorpion sting are emergencies.
Keep the bitten limb still and below the level of the heart if possible.
Remove rings, watches, and tight clothing near the bite before swelling starts.
Note the time of the bite and the appearance of the bite site.
If a bee sting, scrape the sting out sideways with a firm edge (e.g. a card). Do not use tweezers.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Tweezers squeeze more venom from the sac.

actions_to_avoid: Do not cut the bite or try to suck out the venom.
Do not apply a tight tourniquet — it can cause limb loss.
Do not give alcohol, stimulants, or any medication.
Do not apply ice or cold packs to a snakebite.
Do not try to catch or kill the snake — a photo from a safe distance is enough.

escalation_conditions.condition: Difficulty breathing, facial swelling, or collapse
escalation_conditions.action: Call 112; suspect anaphylaxis; if the person has an adrenaline auto-injector and is trained, help them use it
Hospital urgently; antivenom may be needed

escalation_conditions.condition: Person becomes unconscious and stops breathing

approved_alternatives.alternative: If trained and the region has neurotoxic snakes (e.g. mamba, cobra), apply a firm bandage over the bite and up the limb, immobilise with a splint. Do not use for viper bites (causes swelling).

follow_up_requirements: All snakebites need hospital assessment, even if symptoms are mild initially.

age_specific_pathways.child: Children are at higher risk from the same venom dose — urgent assessment.
age_specific_pathways.infant: All bites/stings in infants need urgent hospital care.

source_references.document: International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines
Guidelines for the Management of Snakebites
